key_insight: DeepEdu-v1 proposes an efficient, scalable agentic LLM system tailored for Vietnamese education, aiming to deliver useful tutoring while keeping data local and aligned with the national curriculum. It bridges the gap between generic cloud chatbots and costly self-hosted solutions by making education-specific AI more practical to deploy.
problem_solved: The paper addresses two major barriers to AI tutoring in Vietnam: privacy and sovereignty concerns from sending student data to foreign cloud servers, and poor curriculum alignment from Western-centric pre-trained models that often hallucinate or miss local textbook content.
method: Builds an agentic LLM framework designed specifically for Vietnamese educational use cases.
Organizes knowledge around the national textbook curriculum to improve retrieval, grounding, and answer relevance.
Focuses on efficient, scalable deployment so institutions can self-host or locally run the system more feasibly than large general-purpose models.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how to adapt LLMs for local education markets without sacrificing deployment efficiency or data governance. It offers a template for building culturally and curriculum-aware AI systems that are more trustworthy and usable in regulated settings.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline showing generic cloud chatbot vs. DeepEdu-v1 localized workflow
Map or icon set highlighting data sovereignty and local deployment
Curriculum alignment diagram linking textbook topics to model knowledge sources
Comparison chart of privacy, hallucination risk, and deployment cost
paper_title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education
paper_authors: Quang Nguyen, Hieu Nguyen, Hien Hoang, Toan Pham, Cong Tran
